outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning (Case Type: Conditional Use) for a restaurant use at 3034 24th Street. What to say: Submit the CUA application with a project narrative explaining that the concept is a neighborhood-serving restaurant with limited cooking, no alcohol service, and hours closing before midnight. Emphasize that the use is food-focused (not a bar) and is consistent with the pattern of restaurant approvals on the 24th Street corridor over the last 30 years. Include a floor plan, elevations if the façade changes, a menu or concept description, and photographs of the existing conditions. State that the business is independently owned (not formula retail) if that is the case. Request any fee waiver (e.g. First Year Free) if the operator qualifies. The application fee is approximately $3,100 for a CUA with no construction, adjusted annually for CPI.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Conduct the required pre-application community meeting and post the 30-day notice at the property and mail it to owners and occupants within 300 feet. What to say: SF Planning will schedule or instruct you to hold a community meeting before the hearing. Invite neighbors, the neighborhood association and nearby businesses. Present the concept, emphasize the food focus, the lack of alcohol and late-night hours, and the commitment to good-neighbor practices (sidewalk maintenance, garbage management, odor control, soundproofing). Solicit feedback and address concerns. Post the yellow notice at the property for 30 days and mail it to all owners and occupants within 300 feet per Planning Code § 311. Bring proof of mailing and posting to the hearing.
outcomes.note: The record mentions a post-approval community liaison requirement but does not state pre-application meeting, 30-day notice, 300-foot mailing, or Planning Code § 311 requirements.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Appear at the Planning Commission hearing and present the project. What to say: At the hearing (typically 6–10 months after filing), present the concept as a neighborhood-serving restaurant that fits the corridor's 30-year pattern of food-service approvals. Reference comparable approvals (2015-002658CUA-02 approved February 2025 at 2937 24th St, 2018-013158CUA approved 2019 at 2956 24th St, and 2011.0496C approved 2011 at 2962 24th St). Commit to the expected conditions: hours to 2 AM or earlier, odor control equipment, soundproofing, sidewalk maintenance within one block, garbage kept inside, and a community liaison. If the Commission requests modifications, agree to reasonable conditions and ask for approval subject to those conditions.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with SF Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements and change of use, after Planning Commission approval. What to say: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the kitchen layout, equipment, finishes, plumbing, electrical and mechanical systems. Include the occupant load calculation and the occupancy group classification. Request routing to DPH for plan check, Fire for hood suppression review if applicable, and Planning for zoning conformance review per § 175. The building permit is referred to Planning, which will confirm that the work conforms to the approved CUA. Coordinate plan check comments with your architect and respond promptly to expedite approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit a Public Health plan check application concurrently with or immediately after the building permit application. What to say: File the DPH plan check application online through the Environmental Health portal with two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, a menu, and the business registration number. The fee is $828 for a small remodel or $2,207 for a new restaurant (FY 2026–27). DPH will review the kitchen layout, equipment, finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and compliance with the California Retail Food Code. Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% completion and a final inspection before opening. Book inspections at least two weeks in advance with your plan reviewer.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the final DPH and DBI inspections pass, apply for the Health Permit to Operate online. What to say: Submit the Permit to Operate application with your business registration number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), federal EIN, and proof that at least one certified food safety manager is on staff. The application fee is $470 (FY 2026–27); the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28. DPH will issue the permit after confirming the facility matches the approved plans and the manager certification is on file. The permit must be posted at the premises before opening to the public.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 165 to 435 days. Estimated government cost: $5,600 to $19,300. Notes: These figures are the time to approval and government cost for the Conditional Use Authorization, Health permit to operate, and Building permit with change of use, drawn from the catalog and comparable cases. Time: 165–435 days is the range from filing to approval. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days from filing to Commission approval (catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization), with one comparable decided in 408 days (2018-013158CUA, filed Sept 2018, decided Nov 2019) and another in 20 days (2015-002658CUA-02, filed Dec 2024, decided Feb 2025, though that was an extension of a prior authorization). Add 14–120 days for the building permit and 14–45 days for the health permit, which can run in parallel after CUA approval. Cost: $5,600–$19,300 covers CUA application ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500), DPH Permit to Operate ($470), and building permit fees ($800–$15,000 as a percentage of construction valuation). Not included: business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70–$150), architect and consultant fees, construction costs, or the time to resolve the 2009 building violations if they remain open. The Calle 24 SUD frontage calculation may prohibit the project entirely; obtain that determination before filing.
